sanskrit: rūpam ekaḥ pary abhavad rājā nāmaika ucyate | patīrūpasyaiko rūpaṃ rūpam ekaḥ sukṛtvanām ||
english: One encompassed form entire; one is called King by name; one is lord of form, its very form; one is the form of those who act aright.

sanskrit: prajāpatiḥ parameṣṭhī mṛtyur viśvānaraḥ svaḥ | sarasvānasyā yajñasya vaśāyā adhi jajñire ||
english: Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, Mṛtyu, Viśvānara, and Svarga — from this sacrifice, from this vaśā, were they born.

sanskrit: yasya gṛha ādāyeta vaśā devakṛtaṃ haviḥ | nidhānam asyā eṣyaṃ duhitre patyām iva ||
english: In whose house the vaśā were received as an oblation fashioned by the gods — the treasure to be sought of her is like a daughter's to her husband.

sanskrit: nāsyāḥ sakṛd abhi tiṣṭhen nāsya śloṇā gṛhe syāt | vaśā kanyeva durmaṅkā- -apacityā vijānatā ||
english: Let no one approach her even once; let no lame creature be in his house — for the vaśā, like an ill-omened maiden, brings ruin upon the knowing man who disregards her.

sanskrit: naināṃ rakṣed brāhmaṇebhyo nāmā vi glāpayāti ca | yatīṃ na pratyāvartayed yasya goṣu vaśā syāt ||
english: He should not withhold her from Brāhmaṇas, nor cause her name to be dishonoured; he should not turn back one who has gone forth — in whose cattle the vaśā may be.

sanskrit: nāsyā vaśām ā rundhed devā manuṣyā uta | vaśaṃ yad anvaid brahmaṇā tasmād eṣābhavad vaśā ||
english: Neither gods nor men shall restrain her vaśā; because she followed the will through brahman — therefore has she become the vaśā.

sanskrit: vaśaṃ kṛṇvānā vaśinīyam āgan padaṃ kalyāṇy avapaśyamānā | aniṣṭyeṣṭim abhijāyamānā yajñasya mātrām abhikalpamānā ||
english: Making the will her own, the auspicious one has arrived at the station proper to the sovereign; being born beyond the unsacrificed sacrifice, she who measures out the measure of the rite.

sanskrit: indravantas te marutas turīyaṃ bhejire vaśe | turīyam ādityā rudrās turīyaṃ vasavo vaśe ||
english: The Maruts who possess Indra — they have partaken of the fourth portion in the vaśā; the Ādityās and Rudras have the fourth portion, the Vasus the fourth, in the vaśā.

sanskrit: turīya bhāja ādityān vaśāyāḥ kavayo viduḥ | athāsyāḥ pathyaikā tanuś catasraś cakl̥pe diśaḥ ||
english: The seers know the Ādityās as sharers of the fourth portion in the vaśā; then her body, as the one path, became arranged as the four quarters.

sanskrit: vaśā panthām anv apaśyan nākapṛṣṭhaṃ svarvidām | ādityā enām anv āyann ṛṣayaś ca tapasvinaḥ ||
english: The vaśā beheld the path, the back of the firmament belonging to those who know heaven; the Ādityās followed after her, and the seers rich in austerity.

sanskrit: padepade kalpayanta ādityāṅgiraso yajuḥ | īḍānā anv āyan vaśān tadaiḍaṃ sāmocyate ||
english: Step by step the Ādityās and the Aṅgirasas arranged the Yajus; those who praise followed after the vaśās — therefore is that called the iḍā-Sāman.

sanskrit: vaśeḍā vaśānumatir vaśām āhuḥ sarasvatīm | virājaṃ manyante vaśāṃ vāg vaśā pṛthivī vaśā ||
english: The vaśā is Iḍā; the vaśā is Anumatī; they call Sarasvatī the vaśā; the vaśā they reckon as Virāj; Speech is the vaśā, the Earth is the vaśā.

sanskrit: vaśā deṣṭrī sinīvālī vaśoṣā nirṛtir vaśā | vaśāyāṃ mṛtyum aviśad ā mṛtyum aviśad vaśā ||
english: The vaśā is the guide Sinīvālī; the vaśā is Uṣas; Nirṛti is the vaśā; Death entered into the vaśā — yes, Death entered the vaśā.

sanskrit: agnir vāg udakaṃ cakṣur mano vāto vaśī vaśā | tanvaṃ ko asyās taṃ veda yayodakrāmad ekayā ||
english: Agni, Speech, Water, Eye, Mind, Wind — the sovereign vaśā is the vaśā. Who knows that body of hers wherewith she has stepped forth as the one?

sanskrit: yāṃ cakṣuṣā manasā saṃvidānā hṛdā paśyanti kavayo manīṣinaḥ | tasyāḥ prajādhipatiḥ paśūnāṃ vaśā rājñā nāṃtaveṣā sṛṣṭiḥ ||
english: Her whom the seers, the wise ones, behold in unison with eye, mind, and heart — of her is the lord of the creation of cattle; the vaśā is sovereign: this creation has no boundary-garment.

sanskrit: ko vaśāyā ūdho veda ka ulbaṃ ca jarāyu ca | stanān asyāḥ ko veda ka i tad veda yad duhe ||
english: Who knows the udder of the vaśā? Who knows her amnion and caul? Who knows her teats? Who, indeed, knows that which she yields when milked?

sanskrit: aham asyā ūdho veda- -aham ulbaṃ ca jarāyu ca | stanān asyā ahaṃ veda- -atho tad veda yad duhe ||
english: I know the udder of her; I know her amnion and caul; I know her teats — and I know that which she yields when milked.

sanskrit: nainām̐ ahaṃ rakṣeyaṃ dadyām eva syāc ca me | stanā hy asyā ahaṃ veda kṣīram ulbaṃ ca jarāyu ca ||
english: I would not protect her; yet should she be given, and should she be mine — for I know her teats, her milk, her amnion and her caul.

sanskrit: kṛttir yonir adhivāso jarāyu pāṇḍam ulbaṃ nābhir uṣṇīṣam asyāḥ | ā jarasaṃ dhayatu mātaraṃ vaśī brahmabhiḥ kl̥ptaḥ sa hy asya bandhuḥ ||
english: Skin, womb, covering-garment, caul, pallid amnion, navel, and turban are hers; let the sovereign vaśī suckle the mother to old age — for he who is fashioned by brahman-spells is truly her kinsman.

sanskrit: indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ yāni cakāra prathamāni vajrī | ahann ahim anv apas tatarda pra vakṣaṇā abhinat parvatānām ||
english: Now shall I proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, the first deeds the Vajra-bearer performed: he smote the serpent, then pierced open the waters; he cleft the flanks of the mountains.

sanskrit: ahann ahiṃ parvate śiśriyāṇaṃ tvaṣṭāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa | vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ syandamānā añjaḥ samudram ava jagmur āpaḥ ||
english: He smote the serpent that lay sprawled upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭar had fashioned for him the resonant bolt of heaven. Like lowing cows flowing swiftly, the waters straightway descended to the sea.

sanskrit: vṛṣāyamāṇo 'vṛṇīta somaṃ trikadrukeṣv apibat sutasya | ā sāyakaṃ maghavādatta vajram ahann enaṃ prathamajām ahīnam ||
english: Exerting himself as a bull he chose Soma; he drank of the pressed draught at the three Kadrū-pressings; Maghavan took up the missile, the thunderbolt, and smote that first-born among serpents.

sanskrit: yad indrāhan prathamajām ahīnām ān māyinām amināḥ prota māyāḥ | āt sūryaṃ janayan dyām uṣāsaṃ tādītnā śatruṃ na kilā vivitse ||
english: When, O Indra, thou smotest the first-born among serpents and then destroyed the māyās of the māyā-wielders, bringing forth the sun, the sky, and the dawn — then, verily, thou foundest no enemy to match thee.

sanskrit: ahan vṛtraṃ vṛtrataraṃ vyaṃsam indro vajreṇa mahatā vadhena | skadhāṃsīva kuliśenā vivṛkṇā- -ahiḥ śayad upapṛk pṛthivyāḥ ||
english: Indra smote Vṛtra, the greater of obstructors, the shoulderless one, with the great death-weapon, the thunderbolt; like the branches of a tree split by an axe, the serpent lay stretched along the earth.

sanskrit: ayoddheva durmada ā hi juhve mahāvīraṃ tu vibādham ṛjīṣam | nātārīd asya samṛtiṃ vadhānāṃ saṃ rujānāḥ pipiṣa indraśatruḥ ||
english: For like one drunk with ill-madness he challenged the great hero, the overpowering, the pressers-juice-drinker; the enemy of Indra could not cross the meeting-point of his death-blows — crashing together, he was crushed.

sanskrit: apād ahasto apṛtanyad indram āsya vajram adhi sānau jaghāna | vṛṣṇo vadhriḥ pratimānaṃ babhūṣan purutrā vṛtro aśayad vyastaḥ ||
english: Footless and handless he gave battle to Indra; Indra struck the thunderbolt upon his back's ridge; the castrated one seeking to match the bull — Vṛtra lay strewn in many places, scattered asunder.

sanskrit: nadaṃ na bhinnam amuyā śayānaṃ mano ruhāṇā ati yanty āpaḥ | yāś cid vṛtro mahinā paryatiṣṭhat tāsām ahiḥ patsutaḥśīr babhūva ||
english: Like a broken reed he lay there prostrate; the waters pass over him, rising and climbing in their minds. Over those very waters which Vṛtra in his greatness had encompassed, the serpent became one whose head is crushed underfoot.

sanskrit: nicāvayā abhavad vṛtraputra- -indro asyā ava vadhar jabhāra | uttarā sūr adharaḥ putra āsīd dānuḥ śaye sahavatsā na dhenuḥ ||
english: The mother of Vṛtra was brought low — Indra seized the weapon away from her; the mother was above, the son was below; Dānu lies there like a cow with her calf beside her.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhantīnām aniveśanānāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīram | vṛkasya niṇyaṃ vi caranty āpo dīrghaṃ tama āśayad indraśatruḥ ||
english: Among the currents that stand still, that find no resting-place, the body was laid in the midst of the flood-channels; the waters flow about the secret of the wolf — the enemy of Indra lay stretched in long darkness.
